summary: Describes a profile of the Sieve notification extension for sending notifications over XMPP, also known as Jabber. This is a Proposed Standard.

eli5.summary: This is another way the new-mail ping can reach you: as a quick chat message through an instant messaging system.

questions: how to send sieve notifications over jabber
what is the xmpp uri scheme in sieve
subtitle: How a Sieve mail filter can ping you with an XMPP (Jabber) instant message when new mail arrives.

tldr.problem: The Sieve notification extension sends alerts through pluggable methods named by URIs, and it needs a method that delivers them over XMPP instant messaging.
tldr.mechanism: An xmpp URI in the notify action names the recipient. The Sieve engine turns the notification into an XMPP message stanza with a body, an optional subject, an optional link to the mail and optional headers carrying the sender and urgency.
tldr.outcome: The method is registered with IANA under the name xmpp, so Sieve scripts can send notifications to Jabber accounts.

facts.label: Retry limit
facts.value: Configurable, no less than 3 and no more than 10

today: RFC 5437 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It depends on the Sieve notification framework in RFC 5435.

sections.title: What This Notification Method Is
sections.content:
The notification extension for the Sieve mail filtering language provides a framework for alerts, using URIs to say which notification mechanism to use. RFC 5437 defines how xmpp URIs are used to send those alerts through the Extensible Messaging and Presence Protocol (XMPP), which is widely implemented in Jabber instant messaging technologies.

The RFC inherits its terminology from the Sieve, notification and XMPP specifications, and the key words MUST and SHOULD carry their usual RFC 2119 meaning.
sections.eli5: A mail filter can already tap you on the shoulder when mail arrives. This document says how the tap can be a chat message.

sections.title: Method Parameter and Tags
sections.content:
The notify method parameter MUST be a URI in the xmpp scheme that identifies the XMPP account tied to the email inbox. It MAY include a resource identifier or a query component, but SHOULD NOT include an authority component or fragment identifier. The XMPP address extracted from it becomes the to attribute of the notification.

The tags behave as follows:

  • :from must be an email address matching the RFC 5321 Mailbox rule. It MAY appear in the message text or in a SHIM header named Resent-From.
  • :importance has no special meaning, but it MAY be sent as a SHIM header named Urgency: high for 1, medium for 2 and low for 3.
  • :message MUST become the character data of the XMPP body element.
  • :options has no special meaning here.

For the online capability test, an implementation SHOULD answer yes if it knows of an active presence session and otherwise maybe.
sections.eli5: The address says who gets the chat message. The other settings let the script add a note, say how urgent it is, and say who the mail was from.

sections.title: The Resulting XMPP Message
sections.content:
The notification MUST be an XMPP message stanza. Its from SHOULD be the XMPP address of the notification service tied to the Sieve engine (or of the entity to be notified) and MUST NOT be generated from the Sieve :from tag. Its to MUST be the address from the URI, and its type MUST be headline or normal.

The stanza MUST have a body. The body comes from :message if given, otherwise from a body key in the URI query, otherwise from configurable text saying it is a Sieve notification. A subject element is optional and follows the URI's subject key or configurable text. The stanza SHOULD also carry a URI, inside an x element in the jabber:x:oob namespace, as a hint to locate the message. It SHOULD be an IMAP URL, but MAY be another type such as an HTTP or POP3 URI.
sections.eli5: The chat message has a title, a short note and a link that points back to the real email, like a sticky note saying where to find the letter.

sections.title: Worked Examples
sections.content:
The RFC gives four examples using a sender at juliet@example.org and a recipient whose XMPP address is romeo@im.example.com. The basic form, notify "xmpp:romeo@im.example.com", yields a headline message whose body and subject come from engine configuration, plus a link to the message.

When both a :message tag and a URI body key are present, the tag overrides the key. With :importance "1" the message carries an Urgency header of high, and with a :from tag it also carries a Resent-From header holding that address.
sections.eli5: The examples show a script and the chat message it produces, so you can see how each setting changes the message.

sections.title: Conformance to Notification Requirements
sections.content:
The RFC answers each requirement the Sieve notification framework sets for a method. An implementation SHOULD NOT shorten the final notification text, though a deployment MAY, for example when recipients pay per character. An implementation MAY ignore :from, :importance and :options, and MUST ignore URI actions or keys it does not understand. It MUST NOT add extraneous information beyond the notify parameters.

For failures, it SHOULD NOT retry after an XMPP error of type auth or cancel, and MAY retry after wait. Retries SHOULD be limited to a configurable number no less than 3 and no more than 10, and notifications MAY be throttled if there are too many.
sections.eli5: The rules say how careful to be: do not change the message, ignore settings you do not know, and do not keep retrying forever if the chat system says no.

sections.title: Security and Internationalization
sections.content:
Sending a notification can be comparable to forwarding mail, so care must be taken that confidential information is not sent into an insecure environment. The notification service MUST NOT auto-reply to XMPP messages, which prevents one kind of notification loop. Forwarding loops are not possible because XMPP does not forward messages between addresses.

The online test relies on XMPP presence. A Sieve engine MUST NOT use a user's presence when running scripts for a different script owner, unless it knows that owner is authorized to see it. On the internationalization side, the method value MUST be a URI rather than an IRI, and all data sent over XMPP MUST be encoded in UTF-8.
sections.eli5: A chat ping can reveal private mail details, so be careful what you put in it, and never let the notifier talk back to itself in an endless loop.

sections.title: IANA Registration
sections.content: The RFC registers a new Sieve notification mechanism named xmpp. The mechanism URI is given as RFC 5122, the mechanism-specific options are none, and the permanent reference is RFC 5437.
sections.eli5: The new notification type was written into an official list under the name xmpp.

viz.caption: BASIC ACTION AND RESULTING STANZA (RFC 5437, SECTION 3.1)

data.title: Basic notify action and the XMPP message it might produce
data.code:
notify "xmpp:romeo@im.example.com"

<message from='notify.example.com'
         to='romeo@im.example.com'
         type='headline'
         xml:lang='en'>
  <subject>SIEVE</subject>
  <body><juliet@example.com> You got mail.</body>
  <x xmlns='jabber:x:oob'>
    <url>
      imap://romeo@example.com/INBOX;UIDVALIDITY=385759043/;UID=18
    </url>
  </x>
</message>
